Task for gpt-6.1-sol xhigh: implement/build OFFLINE a minimal FS read service diagnostic, not a performance optimization, from the completed FS06 B frozen pair. Root alone owns hardware/UART/USB/network/credentials. Do not touch these, do not flash/run board tools. Own ONLY a new backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-fs-read-service directory and isolated source/build beneath it. No maintained source or prior frozen artifacts modified. Read root README, korvo-fs-stdio-seek/ab-06-analysis.md, diagnostics README and frozen B code/config before editing.

Authoritative B pair openvela-dev/out/esp32s31-korvo-stdioseek-b-20261023: lib_fseeko only platform change from A. FS06 default1000 reads57.581ms vsA66.666, fd replay40.838ms, FILE replay48.333ms; PRNG2.607ms. Read phase only5 software flash reads6144B and no explicit FLASHHW read/pp/erase; replay phases zero FLASHIO. Need distinguish cached LFS/VFS service from user/kernel boundary, before designing larger buffers. Keep all original workloads, PRNG,64B FILE,20B fd requests, config, cache/pool, synchronization and error behavior unchanged. Original numbered5.1.7 source/object stays unchanged.

Implement fixed cumulative read/seek call count, requested/completed bytes, operation error counts and hardware wall time for littlefs_read/seek. Split mount mutex acquisition wait from held service. In node_read, count page-hit vs fallback LFS seek/read calls/bytes. Use the existing SMP-safe ESP32S31 hardware time API esp32s31_timer_diag_time_us, not cross-CPU cycles or10ms clock. Snapshot via the existing /dev/s31stat formatter, no new ioctl/protocol/app workload, no per-operation output, no heap/thread/cache additions. Counters may aggregate FS activity; make their scope explicit. Prefer simple fixed counters under existing mount lock plus minimal short snapshot protection to ensure64bit coherence; do not nest a new global lock across mount lock or IO. Include failed lock/invalid-call accounting without changing returns or errno. If exact PID/file filtering is needed, stop and explain; don't build a broad tracing framework. Measure/calculate instrumentation sample overhead separately; an added measurement cannot be silently subtracted or called pureCPUtime.

Read FS06 diagnostics/readpath.inc: it already captures /dev/s31stat before/after each phase including empty, setup, originalread, PRNG,FILE/fd replay, write, commit, verify. Preserve these buffers and app unchanged if snapshot output still fits. Verify actual stored/truncation contract. Output counters in a small fixed number of lines (counts, bytes, wait/held/total times, per-layer optional counters); reset not needed because phase differences suffice. Document timings include preemption; sums are not automatically total syscall time and cross-phase cached history differs. Preserve raw calibration.

Use meaningful actual-function host tests for return/state/IO order unchanged and counters on success/failure/short-read/page-hit/fallback/invalidseek, plus timestamp arithmetic/snapshot coherence if applicable. No duplicate low-value tests. Full locked isolated target build/pair, correct9 absolute symlink rebasing, config/source/output hashes and diff scope, actual target sizes/stack. No dependency updates/downloads. Final receipt compatible with existing flash consumer; board adapter preparation is a later Root decision. Leave original passed functionality and protection evidence intact. Report earliest concrete issues, then complete code/tests/build and handoff.

I’ll inspect the frozen B sources, snapshot contract, and local instructions first, then build the diagnostic offline in the new owned directory. I won’t access hardware, UART, USB, network, or credentials.

The FS06 app already stores 8192 bytes per snapshot, matching the formatter’s buffer. Its length check does not detect the formatter’s `truncated=1` marker, so I’ll test the actual formatter size and truncation behavior while preserving the app and its buffers.

I’ll aggregate counters across all LittleFS mounts. Each call will collect its measurements locally and publish them under a short snapshot lock after releasing the mount mutex; that lock will never span mutex acquisition or I/O.

Frozen B is copied, and all nine absolute source symlinks now resolve inside the isolated tree. The diagnostic adds four report lines for read calls, seek calls, node page/fallback activity, and raw empty-instrumentation calibration.

Timing will use the existing SMP-safe hardware clock. The report will document that these are wall times, include preemption, and end before counter publication. I’ll now check behavior against the frozen functions and start the full target build.

The first target compile caught an insertion error in the read hook: the edit script matched the declaration instead of the function body. I corrected the script, reapplied the overlay from frozen B, and retained the failed log. The build is continuing; no frozen or maintained files changed.

The complete target build passed. The host checks also passed: 21 cases compare frozen and instrumented function bodies for returns, positions, sticky errors, errno, and lock/LFS call order. A concurrent check exercised 40,000 publications and coherent snapshots across a 32-bit carry.

I’m now checking the actual formatter and FS06 storage path with large counter values, then reviewing object hashes, target sizes, and stack frames.

The actual formatter, its existing subformatters, device read, and unchanged FS06 sampler passed the storage check. With maximum-width counters, all 16 queue slots, 12 waiters, and 16 backtrace entries, the report stored 7,301 bytes including NUL, leaving 891 bytes free. The explicit truncation marker also passed its saturation test.

The clean full rebuild completed under an exclusive lock. The object review found exactly two changes: the LittleFS VFS object and the existing status formatter object. All app objects, including numbered 5.1.7, match frozen B.

Verification is nearly complete. The diagnostic adds 2,640 bytes of target text and 496 bytes of fixed BSS; data size is unchanged. All 21 application ELFs and the AppFS image are byte-identical to B. Target stack frames are recorded, and the diagnostic and numbered test still declare 32 KiB stacks.

The final audit is rechecking frozen B and the prior protection hashes before publishing the receipt and handoff. Hardware timing values remain for Root to collect.

Implemented and completed the locked offline build in the owned directory.

- Added four cumulative status lines covering read/seek counts, bytes, errors, mutex wait/held/total wall time, node hits/fallbacks, and raw calibration.
- Passed 21 differential function cases and 40,000 concurrent publications.
- Verified the unchanged 8192-byte snapshot contract; worst-width report leaves 891 bytes free.
- Reviewed all 3343 objects: only VFS and formatter differ. Configuration, numbered 5.1.7, all 21 app ELFs, AppFS, and protected evidence remain unchanged.
- Target increase: 2640 B text and 496 B BSS. Stack frames are documented.

[Handoff and limitations](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-fs-read-service/README.md) · [Final pair receipt](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-fs-read-service/final-receipt.json)

No hardware interfaces were accessed. Board timing and adapter preparation remain Root’s later decision.
